title: Linkability of submissions across courses and sessions
description: The portal can link the student's identity, assignment file, course, login event, and submission timestamp across multiple submissions and courses, enabling profiling of the student's behavior and academic activity over time.
assumptions: The web app stores or can access persistent identifiers such as student id and account/session data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering for linkability of data records may vary.

title: Identifiability of the student from submitted data
description: The submitted data directly contains student id and is associated with a login, making the student explicitly identifiable in the submission transaction and any related logs or records.
assumptions: Student id is unique and retained by the portal or surrounding infrastructure.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ for direct identifiability.

title: Disclosure of assignment contents and metadata in transit or logs
description: The work file, student id, course, and submission timestamp may be exposed to unauthorized parties if transport protection is weak, endpoints are misconfigured, or application/server logs capture sensitive payloads and metadata.
assumptions: The flow traverses networks and may be logged by the application, reverse proxies, or monitoring systems.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of data in transit/processing; exact numbering may vary.

title: Unawareness of collection and secondary use of submission metadata
description: The student may be unaware that the portal collects not only the assignment file but also identifiers, course information, timestamps, IP/session metadata, and possibly uses them for analytics, retention, plagiarism workflows, or auditing.
assumptions: Privacy notices or just-in-time explanations are incomplete or not salient at submission time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of transparency/awareness; exact numbering may vary.

title: Non-compliance due to excessive collection or retention
description: Collecting and retaining the full assignment file together with student id, course, and precise submission timestamp longer than necessary, or using them beyond grading-related purposes, may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, or retention obligations.
assumptions: Applicable education/privacy rules require minimization, defined purpose, and bounded retention.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for policy/legal non-compliance; exact numbering may vary.

title: Repudiation disputes around submission and receipt
description: If the portal lacks adequate evidence, the student may later deny having submitted a specific file at a specific time, or the portal may be unable to prove what was received, creating disputes that can affect privacy when additional monitoring or logging is introduced to compensate.
assumptions: Submission receipts, integrity checks, or audit trails may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Applicability is moderate because non-repudiation is partly security-oriented; included here due to LINDDUN repudiation concerns. Node id is best-fit.

title: Detectability of student activity from observable submission events
description: Observers such as network intermediaries, shared-device users, or internal operators may be able to detect that a particular student is active and submitting coursework at a specific time, even without accessing the full content.
assumptions: Traffic patterns, notifications, or operational dashboards expose event occurrence metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability of communication/activity; exact numbering may vary.

title: Linkability of student actions across courses and submissions
description: The portal forwards a stable student identifier together with course and file reference to the grading service, enabling correlation of multiple submissions and grading requests belonging to the same student across assignments or courses.
assumptions: The grading service can observe repeated requests over time and the student id is stable across contexts.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via persistent identifiers on an inter-process data flow; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Identifiability of the student in grading requests
description: Including the student id in the routed request makes the data subject directly identifiable to the assignment and grading service, even where grading could potentially be performed with a pseudonymous submission token.
assumptions: The grading service does not strictly require direct identity for every processing step.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for direct identifiability from explicit identifiers in data flow.

title: Disclosure of academic context and submission metadata
description: The flow reveals personal data and educational context, including student id, enrolled course, file reference, and requester role. If intercepted, over-logged, or exposed internally, this can disclose a student's coursework activity and assessment interactions.
assumptions: The flow or its logs may be accessible to unauthorized parties or retained beyond necessity.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for information disclosure on a data flow; exact subtree may differ depending on whether exposure is in transit, logging, or internal access.

title: Disclosure through file reference enabling access to submission content
description: Even if the file itself is not sent, the file reference may permit retrieval or inference of the student's submission content or storage location, exposing additional personal data if mishandled.
assumptions: The file reference is resolvable or meaningful to the receiving service or to an attacker who gains access to logs or messages.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is approximate; threat depends on whether the reference is a capability, path, or otherwise sensitive locator.

title: Insufficient evidence of who initiated submission or grading actions
description: If the routed request does not carry strong, privacy-preserving proof of the requesting role and initiating party, the grading service may be unable to demonstrate whether a student, instructor, or portal component initiated a specific action, enabling repudiation of submissions or grading requests.
assumptions: Requests may rely on weak attribution or mutable application logs rather than signed or tamper-evident records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation due to insufficient evidence on an inter-process request flow.

title: Unawareness of onward processing by grading service
description: Students may be unaware that the portal forwards their identifiers, course context, file reference, and role-related request metadata to a separate grading service, reducing transparency about recipients and processing purposes.
assumptions: The system's notices or UI do not clearly disclose this internal sharing and its purpose.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate for lack of transparency/unawareness regarding data recipients and processing.

title: Excessive data sharing beyond necessity for grading purpose
description: Sending the full student id, course, file reference, and requesting role for every submission or grading request may exceed data minimization requirements if the grading service could operate with less data, such as a pseudonymous submission token or scoped authorization attribute.
assumptions: Not all transmitted attributes are strictly necessary for the grading service's purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with data minimization/purpose limitation; exact subtree may vary.

title: Stored assignment records are linkable across courses and submissions via student identifier
description: The grading service stores assignment files together with a persistent student id, course, and submission time. This enables linking multiple submissions by the same student across assignments and potentially across courses, allowing reconstruction of activity patterns and academic behavior.
assumptions: Student id is stable over time and reused across multiple submissions and courses; DS1 can be queried or accessed in ways that expose these records together.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether linkability is modeled at data-store level or attribute level.

title: Stored metadata can identify a student from assignment records
description: The combination of student id, course, submission time, and assignment file in the assignment store directly identifies the student and ties them to a specific submission. Even if the file content were pseudonymous, the metadata is sufficient for identification.
assumptions: Student id is directly identifying or readily resolvable to a specific student by the system or authorized users.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability from stored data attributes.

title: Assignment store reveals sensitive academic and behavioral information
description: Persisting assignment files with course and submission time may disclose personal information such as academic performance indicators, study habits, deadlines missed, writing style, and potentially special-category or sensitive content contained in submissions.
assumptions: Assignment content and timing are accessible to parties beyond the minimum necessary set, or could be inferred through logs, backups, or secondary use.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node; exact subtree depends on whether disclosure is framed as content, metadata, or excessive access.

title: Stored submission records may be used as evidence without adequate repudiation controls
description: Because the store keeps student id and submission time, the record may later be used to claim that a student submitted or failed to submit at a certain time. If integrity, provenance, or dispute-handling controls are weak, the student may be unable to repudiate an incorrect or manipulated record.
assumptions: Submission timestamps or stored files can be altered, overwritten, or insufficiently audited; disputes about submission timing are relevant.
uncertainty_note: LINDDUN node id is approximate; non-repudiation threats are sometimes modeled differently depending on evidence and logging structure.

title: Students may be unaware that detailed submission metadata and files are retained
description: The flow stores not only the assignment file but also student id, course, and submission time. If retention, access, reuse for analytics, or sharing with instructors and administrators is not transparent, students may lack awareness of how their submission data is processed.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-context explanations are incomplete or absent regarding storage, retention, and downstream use.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node; exact node may differ based on whether the issue is lack of notice, opaque retention, or hidden secondary processing.

title: Storing identifiable submissions may exceed necessity or violate retention/minimization requirements
description: Persisting full assignment files together with direct student identifiers and precise submission times may be more data than necessary for all purposes, especially if long-term retention, broad access, or secondary uses are not justified. This can create non-compliance with data minimization, purpose limitation, or retention obligations.
assumptions: There are applicable privacy requirements or institutional policies limiting retention, identifiability, or secondary use of student submissions.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate because compliance threats depend on the specific legal/policy obligation in scope.

title: Teacher identity disclosure through login request metadata
description: The login and queue-request flow reveals the teacher's identity or account identifier to the web application and potentially to supporting components via usernames, email addresses, session identifiers, IP address, and course-selection context. If exposed beyond what is necessary, this can disclose which teacher is accessing the system.
assumptions: The flow carries teacher credentials or identifiers and request metadata that can be observed, logged, or shared internally.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether identity is disclosed directly or via observable identifiers.

title: Linkability of teacher activities across sessions
description: Repeated login and queue-access requests can be linked together using stable account identifiers, cookies, device fingerprints, or persistent session tokens, allowing the portal or observers with access to logs to correlate the same teacher's review activity over time.
assumptions: The system uses persistent identifiers or logs sufficient metadata to correlate requests across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact subtree depends on whether linkability is via protocol identifiers, application identifiers, or metadata.

title: Detectability of teacher review activity
description: An observer who can see network traffic, access logs, or application telemetry may detect that a teacher is logging in and requesting the submissions queue, thereby learning that the teacher is currently active and performing grading-related work even if the content is protected.
assumptions: Traffic patterns, endpoint names, timing, or logs are visible to some party beyond the teacher.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact subtree depends on whether detectability arises from traffic analysis, endpoint observability, or logging.

title: Teacher actions may be provable to third parties via detailed logs
description: If the portal stores detailed authentication and queue-access logs tied to the teacher identity, those records may later be used to prove that a specific teacher accessed the grading queue at a particular time. This can reduce plausible deniability regarding work patterns or access behavior.
assumptions: The application maintains attributable audit logs and those logs may be disclosed or repurposed.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; non-repudiation is somewhat context-dependent here because auditability may be intentional for security purposes.

title: Excessive collection of teacher data during login and queue request
description: The portal may collect more personal data than necessary for authentication and queue retrieval, such as detailed device information, precise location, behavioral telemetry, or unnecessary course/workload metadata, without a clear necessity for the stated purpose.
assumptions: The application or integrated analytics collect ancillary metadata beyond what is strictly needed to authenticate and return the queue.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact subtree depends on the specific non-compliance category such as data minimization or purpose limitation.

title: Insufficient transparency about monitoring of teacher access
description: The teacher may be unaware of what personal data is processed when logging in and requesting the submissions queue, such as retention of access logs, analytics, device fingerprinting, or sharing with administrators and service providers. This lack of transparency undermines predictability of processing.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-context explanations are incomplete or not presented at the time of collection.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact subtree may differ depending on whether the issue is lack of notice, unclear purposes, or opaque recipients.

title: Disclosure of teacher-course association from queue request
description: The request for the submissions queue can reveal which courses or assessment queues are associated with the teacher. If request parameters, URLs, or logs expose course identifiers, unauthorized parties may infer the teacher's teaching assignments or workload.
assumptions: Course identifiers or queue parameters are included in the request or derived from it and may be visible in logs, URLs, or telemetry.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact subtree depends on whether the disclosure is of attributes, role relationships, or confidential content.

title: Exposure of student identities to an unintended teacher or unauthorized viewer
description: If the portal displays submissions without strong access control or session isolation, a teacher could view student names, work content, and submission times for classes or students they are not authorized to access, disclosing personal data.
assumptions: The web app may rely on role-based access checks and session management to ensure only the correct teacher can view the submissions.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for unauthorized disclosure via data flow; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Linkability of multiple submissions belonging to the same student
description: Displaying student names together with work content and timestamps allows the teacher to link multiple submissions and activities to the same student over time, enabling construction of a behavioral or performance history beyond a single submission event.
assumptions: The portal presents persistent identifiers such as student names consistently across submissions.
uncertainty_note: Linkability is inherent to identified student records in this flow; node id is approximate.

title: Identifiability of students from displayed submission data
description: Student names directly identify the submitting students, and work content plus submission times may further identify them even if names were partially masked. The flow therefore reveals the identity of data subjects to the recipient.
assumptions: Teacher can see explicit names or other unique identifiers in the portal.
uncertainty_note: This is a straightforward identifiability issue, but the exact threat-tree node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Over-disclosure of submission metadata and content
description: The portal may disclose more personal data than necessary to the teacher, such as exact submission times, full work content, or information from students outside the teacher's instructional need, increasing privacy exposure.
assumptions: Not all displayed fields are strictly necessary for the teacher's immediate task.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for excessive data exposure; exact node id uncertain.

title: Teacher can deny having viewed a student's submission
description: If the portal does not maintain reliable viewing logs or acknowledgements, the teacher may later deny having accessed specific student submissions, reducing accountability for access to personal data.
assumptions: The system may lack tamper-resistant audit logs for read access events.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation applicability depends on whether access logging is in scope for this flow; node id is approximate.

title: Teacher may be unaware of why specific student data is shown
description: The portal may present names, content, and timestamps without clear explanation of purpose, retention, or access basis, creating a risk that data processing is insufficiently transparent to the recipient and potentially to the underlying data subjects through the interface behavior.
assumptions: The interface may not explain why each data element is necessary or how it should be handled.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is less direct on this display flow and may be considered weaker than disclosure threats; node id is approximate.

title: Display of student submissions may exceed consent or educational-purpose limitations
description: If students submitted work for a limited educational purpose, showing full content and detailed timestamps to a broader set of teachers or for secondary uses may violate consent expectations, purpose limitation, or other privacy obligations.
assumptions: Applicable legal basis, consent scope, or institutional policy may restrict which teachers can access which submission details.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends heavily on organizational policy and legal basis; exact node id is a best estimate.

title: Teacher identity disclosed with grading action
description: The flow contains grader id together with student id, grade, and feedback. If the web app exposes or stores this data too broadly, recipients can infer which teacher graded which student and assignment, revealing the teacher's involvement in a specific evaluation.
assumptions: Assumes grader identity is visible beyond strictly authorized school staff or is retained in logs/audit views accessible to others.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether identity disclosure is modeled as direct identifier exposure or attribute disclosure.

title: Sensitive academic performance data disclosed
description: The submitted grade and written feedback are personal data about the student and may reveal performance, behavior, or special circumstances. If the web app transmits, logs, or displays this flow insecurely, unauthorized parties could learn the student's assessment details.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient transport protection, excessive internal access, insecure logging, or overbroad display within the portal.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for disclosure of data content in transit/processing.

title: Linkability of student records across assignments and teachers
description: Because the flow includes student id and grader id with each grade submission, the portal can link multiple grading events for the same student across assignments and potentially across teachers, enabling profiling of academic history and teacher-student interactions.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers are persistent and reused across submissions and that the system or insiders can correlate records over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via persistent identifiers; exact subtree may differ.

title: Student identity identifiable from submitted assessment
description: The flow explicitly includes student id alongside grade and feedback, making the assessed student directly identifiable within the portal and any connected logs or downstream components.
assumptions: Assumes the student id is directly identifying within the organization or can be readily mapped to a named student.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability through direct identifiers.

title: Teacher can deny having submitted a grade or feedback
description: If the portal does not create reliable, integrity-protected submission records, a teacher may later dispute having entered a particular grade or comment, undermining accountability and creating privacy risks around contested personal data processing.
assumptions: Assumes weak authentication binding, missing timestamps, editable logs, or lack of non-repudiation controls.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; LINDDUN Pro non-repudiation subtrees vary by sender/receiver repudiation framing.

title: Teacher may be unaware of secondary use or retention of grading data
description: When entering grades and feedback, the teacher may not understand how long the portal retains the data, who can access it, whether comments are visible to students/parents, or whether entries are reused for analytics or performance monitoring.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient just-in-time notice, unclear UI, or opaque backend processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of user awareness/transparency; exact subtree may differ.

title: Collection of excessive personal data in feedback submission
description: The portal may encourage or permit teachers to enter more personal information than necessary in free-text feedback, including sensitive details about the student, causing processing beyond what is necessary for grading.
assumptions: Assumes no minimization controls, guidance, or validation on free-text feedback fields.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data minimization / policy non-compliance; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may vary.

title: Disclosure of grade records from persistent storage
description: The database stores highly sensitive educational records including student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp. If storage access controls, query restrictions, or encryption are insufficient, unauthorized parties could access complete grade records.
assumptions: DS2 persists grade records and may be accessible by administrators, services, or analysts beyond the grading service.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for information disclosure from data at rest; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Linkability of student performance across courses and assessments
description: Because the stored record contains a student identifier together with course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp, records can be linked across courses, terms, or assessment events to build a longitudinal profile of a student's academic performance.
assumptions: The same student id is reused across multiple grade records and can be queried or correlated over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via persistent identifiers in stored records; exact node id may differ in the official tree.

title: Identifiability of students and graders in stored grade records
description: The grade record directly contains student id and grader id, making both data subjects identifiable. Even if names are absent, these identifiers can typically be resolved to individuals through institutional systems.
assumptions: Student id and grader id are unique or readily mappable to real persons within the organization.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for direct identifiability from stored identifiers; exact node id may vary.

title: Detectability of grading events from write timing and record presence
description: The presence of a new record and its timestamp can reveal that a particular student was assessed in a particular course at a particular time, even before the content is viewed. Observers with metadata access could detect grading activity patterns.
assumptions: Some actors can observe record creation events, timestamps, logs, or database metadata without full content access.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability from metadata and event presence; exact node id may differ.

title: Insufficient proof of who assigned or changed a grade
description: Although grader id and timestamp are written, if the service does not create tamper-evident audit trails or strong attribution for the write operation, a grader or operator may later deny having assigned or modified a grade record.
assumptions: The flow writes business data but may not ensure integrity-protected logging or non-repudiation controls for grade submissions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-repudiation gaps in write operations; exact node id may vary.

title: Storage of grade records beyond necessity or without adequate legal basis constraints
description: The database stores detailed grade records including feedback, grader id, and timestamps. If retention periods, purpose limitation, access scope, or lawful-basis constraints are not enforced, the storage and later reuse of these records may violate privacy obligations.
assumptions: No explicit retention, minimization, or purpose-limitation controls are stated for this datastore.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for policy/compliance non-compliance related to retention and purpose limitation; exact node id may differ.

title: Unawareness of how grades, feedback, and grader identifiers are stored and reused
description: Students and graders may be unaware that detailed grade records, feedback text, grader identifiers, and timestamps are persistently stored and potentially reused for analytics, appeals, audits, or reporting.
assumptions: The system description does not mention notices, transparency mechanisms, or user-facing explanations for storage and downstream use.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of transparency/awareness about storage and reuse; exact node id may vary.

title: Portal can identify the requesting student through authenticated grade requests
description: When the student requests grades and feedback, the web app necessarily links the request to a specific student account or identifier. This enables identification of the data subject in connection with highly sensitive academic records.
assumptions: The portal requires login or otherwise receives a student identifier/session tied to the student.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Disclosure of grades and feedback to an unauthorized party
description: If transport security, session handling, or access control is weak, the student's grades and feedback could be exposed to someone other than the student, such as another student or an eavesdropper.
assumptions: The flow carries grades/feedback or triggers retrieval of them over a networked channel.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for unauthorized disclosure/eavesdropping style disclosure.

title: Repeated grade requests can be linked to the same student
description: Multiple requests for grades and feedback can be linked via account identifiers, session cookies, IP/device fingerprints, or stable student IDs, allowing the portal to build a pattern of when and how often a student checks academic results.
assumptions: The portal maintains sessions, logs, or persistent identifiers across requests.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability across interactions; exact subtree label may differ.

title: Excessive request metadata reveals sensitive academic interest
description: Even if the response content is protected, request parameters, URLs, referrers, logs, or analytics may reveal that the student is accessing grades or specific feedback items, disclosing sensitive educational information indirectly.
assumptions: Request paths, query strings, or telemetry/logging capture the purpose or scope of the request.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for indirect/content-adjacent disclosure via metadata.

title: Student may be unable to deny having made a grade request
description: Detailed portal logs can create strong evidence that a particular student requested their grades at a specific time. While useful operationally, this can reduce the student's plausible deniability about accessing sensitive academic information.
assumptions: The system stores attributable audit logs for requests.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation due to attributable logging.

title: Student may be unaware of logging and secondary use of grade-access requests
description: The student may not realize that the portal logs when they request grades and feedback, how often they do so, from which device/location, and that this metadata could be used for analytics, monitoring, or support purposes.
assumptions: The portal collects operational logs or analytics beyond what the student expects.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node naming may vary.

title: Request processing may exceed data minimization or purpose limitation expectations
description: To serve a grade request, the portal might collect or retain more personal data than necessary, such as detailed device fingerprints, precise location, or long-term access logs, potentially conflicting with privacy obligations and user expectations.
assumptions: The implementation collects ancillary telemetry or retains logs beyond the minimum needed to deliver grades.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for non-compliance/privacy requirement violations such as minimization and retention.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades and feedback to someone other than the student
description: If the portal response is delivered to the wrong browser session, exposed through weak access control, or cached/shared on a device, the student's grades and teacher feedback could be seen by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The flow contains personal educational records and narrative feedback, which are sensitive personal data. The portal may be accessed from shared or unmanaged devices.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for disclosure of data in transit/output to an unauthorized recipient; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Student can be identified through the grade display content
description: The displayed grades and teacher feedback directly relate to a specific student account and may include identifying details, making the student identifiable to anyone who can view the screen or captured output.
assumptions: The student is authenticated or otherwise associated with a unique account/session when viewing the portal.
uncertainty_note: Identification is inherent in this flow, but the exact threat-tree node id may differ depending on whether LINDDUN Pro models direct identifiers in content versus context.

title: Viewing events for grades may be linkable across sessions or contexts
description: Repeated delivery of grades and feedback through the portal can allow the service or observers with access to logs, browser artifacts, or network metadata to link multiple grade-viewing events to the same student over time.
assumptions: The portal or surrounding infrastructure logs requests, session identifiers, timestamps, or device/browser metadata.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible linkability threat arising from repeated access patterns; exact node id is approximate.

title: Excessive detail in teacher feedback may disclose more personal data than necessary
description: Teacher feedback shown alongside grades may contain unnecessary sensitive details about behavior, health, accommodations, or personal circumstances, exceeding what is necessary for the student-facing purpose.
assumptions: Free-text feedback may be authored without strict minimization guidance or review.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/disclosure distinction can vary by LINDDUN Pro version; node id is approximate for content overexposure/excessive disclosure.

title: Student may be unable to prove what grades or feedback were shown
description: If the portal does not provide reliable records, timestamps, or receipts of what was displayed, the student may later be unable to demonstrate that a particular grade or feedback item was presented or changed.
assumptions: Grades or feedback may be updated after publication and the portal may not preserve a user-visible history.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation-related node id is my best estimate for lack of evidence of data communication/display.

title: Displaying grades and feedback without adequate transparency or legal basis information
description: If the portal shows educational records without clear notice about purposes, retention, recipients, or student rights, the processing associated with this disclosure may fail compliance expectations for transparency and lawful handling of student data.
assumptions: Applicable education/privacy rules require transparency and appropriate governance for student records.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance applicability depends on jurisdiction and institutional obligations; node id is approximate.

title: Parent account login can identify the requesting parent and link them to a specific child
description: When the parent logs in and requests grades, the web app can directly identify the parent account and associate it with the linked child account and the child's academic records. This creates a privacy risk if identification is unnecessary beyond authorization or if identifiers are exposed internally or in logs.
assumptions: The portal stores a persistent parent account linked to a child account and processes the request using account identifiers.

title: Login and grade-request events enable linkage between parent and child profiles
description: The act of logging in and requesting a child's grades allows the system to link the parent's identity, the child account, and the specific educational record access event. Repeated accesses can build a detailed relationship graph and behavioral profile of the family.
assumptions: The application records account relationships and access events over time.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability arising from correlating identities/accounts and events.

title: Grade request reveals sensitive information about the child to the service
description: By requesting grades, the parent discloses that they are interested in a particular child and causes the child's academic performance data to be processed in connection with the parent account. This may reveal sensitive educational information and family relationship information to backend components, operators, or logs beyond what is strictly necessary.
assumptions: Educational records are privacy-sensitive and request metadata may be logged or observable by administrators/support staff.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of content/attributes during transmission and processing; exact subtree may differ.

description: If the portal lacks strong, privacy-respecting audit evidence, a parent could deny initiating the login or grade request. Conversely, overly detailed non-repudiation logs may themselves create privacy risks by permanently recording access to a child's grades.
assumptions: The system may need auditability for access to student records.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit because non-repudiation trees vary and this flow raises both lack-of-proof and over-logging concerns.

description: The parent may not understand what personal data are collected during login and grade requests, such as IP address, device/browser fingerprint, timestamps, relationship to the child, and access history, nor how long such data are retained or shared.
assumptions: The portal collects standard web authentication and access telemetry.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for insufficient transparency / lack of awareness; exact node naming may differ.

title: Parent-child account linkage and grade access may exceed consent or authorization expectations
description: The portal may process the child's grades based on the parent's linked account without adequately validating legal authority, custody status, age-of-majority rules, or the child's own privacy rights. This can create non-compliance with consent, educational privacy, or data minimization obligations.
assumptions: Access rights may depend on jurisdiction, custody arrangements, and student age/status.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance related to consent/legitimate authorization; exact subtree may vary.

title: Credentials and request details could be exposed from the parent side during transmission
description: As the parent submits login credentials and a request for the child's grades, those data may be exposed if the parent uses an insecure device, shared browser, autofill, malicious extensions, or an inadequately protected connection. Exposure can reveal both the parent's identity and the child's educational information request.
assumptions: The flow includes credential submission and a web request over the network from a user-controlled device.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for disclosure in transit/from the user's endpoint rather than the server side.

title: Parent can identify detailed academic performance of the child
description: The portal reveals the child's grades, teacher feedback, and submission history to the parent. This exposes directly identifying and highly specific educational performance information about the child to another party.
assumptions: Assumes the child is a distinct data subject from the parent and that the portal presents record-level academic data tied to that child.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best-fit estimate for identifiability via direct disclosure of personal data; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Disclosure of sensitive educational records to an unauthorized parent
description: If access control or session handling is weak, the portal may display the child's grades, feedback, and submission history to a parent who is not authorized to view that child's records, disclosing confidential educational information.
assumptions: Assumes risk of broken authorization, account sharing, or misbinding of parent-child relationships in the portal.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unauthorized disclosure from the process on this flow; exact node id may differ in the LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: Parent can deny having viewed the child's academic records
description: If the system does not maintain adequate viewing logs or evidence, a parent may later deny having accessed grades, feedback, or submission history, undermining accountability for access to the child's educational data.
assumptions: Assumes access events are relevant for accountability and may need to be evidenced.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for repudiation of having performed a data access action.

title: Insufficient transparency about what academic data is shown and why
description: The portal may present grades, feedback, and submission history to the parent without clearly informing them and the child about the scope of data shown, the source of the data, retention period, or the basis on which the parent is entitled to access it.
assumptions: Assumes the interface may omit privacy notices or contextual explanations for this disclosure.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact subtree id may vary.

title: Sharing full submission history with the parent may exceed necessity or consent expectations
description: Displaying the complete submission history and detailed feedback to the parent may go beyond what is necessary for the stated purpose, or may conflict with policy, consent, age-appropriate privacy expectations, or educational data protection obligations.
assumptions: Assumes applicable rules may limit parental visibility based on necessity, child age, school policy, or jurisdiction.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for non-compliance with data minimization/purpose limitation or lawful-basis constraints.

title: Repeated portal views enable linkage of the child's academic events over time
description: By showing grades, feedback, and submission history together, the portal enables the parent or anyone observing the account to link multiple academic events across time into a detailed profile of the child's behavior and performance.
assumptions: Assumes historical records are aggregated and persistently associated with the same child account.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability through aggregation/history display; exact node id may differ.

title: Detailed academic history allows inference of private traits or circumstances
description: Grades, teacher feedback, and submission patterns may allow the parent or an unintended viewer to infer sensitive information such as learning difficulties, health issues, behavioral concerns, family circumstances, or disabilities beyond the explicitly displayed data.
assumptions: Assumes feedback and submission patterns are sufficiently detailed to support such inferences.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability/discoverability via inference from exposed records; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary.

title: Exposure of account and family-relationship data to unauthorized portal staff or functions
description: The flow carries names, emails, roles, account status changes, and parent-child relationship updates from the administrator into the web app. If the portal does not strictly enforce authorization and purpose limitation on receipt and processing of this administrative input, internal components or privileged users could access or infer sensitive relationship and role information beyond what they need.
assumptions: The web app stores or routes the submitted administrative data to backend components and administrative interfaces where access control may be imperfect.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id selected from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Over-collection or excessive retention of administrator-submitted identity and relationship data
description: Creating and modifying accounts and parent-child links may result in the portal collecting more personal data than necessary for account administration, or retaining historical relationship/account-change records longer than needed. This can disclose unnecessary details about students, parents, and staff over time.
assumptions: The portal persists submitted fields and possibly audit/history records for operational convenience.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort approximation from memory; exact retention/minimization subtree may differ.

title: Linkability of individuals across accounts and family relationships
description: The administrator explicitly manages parent-child links and account-role assignments. Within the portal, these updates can enable linking student, parent, and administrator-related records across contexts, making it easier to correlate identities, household relationships, and role histories than data subjects may expect.
assumptions: The portal maintains identifiers that allow records and relationship changes to be correlated over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro linkability subtree may differ.

title: Insufficient transparency to parents and students about account and relationship changes
description: When an administrator creates, modifies, or disables accounts and parent-child links, affected data subjects may not be informed that their personal data and relationships were changed, what fields were changed, or why. Lack of notice reduces awareness of processing and may hide impactful administrative actions.
assumptions: The portal may not automatically notify affected users or provide visible change history.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id selected from memory; exact detectability/disclosure subtree may differ.

title: Unawareness of downstream use of administrative identity data
description: Data subjects whose names, emails, roles, and family links are entered or changed by the administrator may be unaware of how the portal uses this information, such as authentication, notifications, access decisions, reporting, or synchronization with other school systems.
assumptions: The portal uses the submitted data for multiple operational purposes not fully visible to affected users.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro unawareness subtree may differ.

title: Administrative account and relationship management may violate consent or legal-basis constraints
description: Parent-child links and account status changes can materially affect access to student information. If the portal accepts or applies these changes without verifying the appropriate legal basis, authority, or consent status, processing may be non-compliant with privacy obligations governing minors' data and family relationships.
assumptions: Applicable policy or law requires a valid basis and authorized role for establishing or removing family relationships and related access.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id selected from memory; exact non-compliance subtree may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence of who performed account and relationship changes
description: If the portal does not create reliable, tamper-evident logs for administrator actions on accounts and parent-child links, the administrator could later deny having created, modified, or disabled an account or relationship. This undermines accountability for privacy-impacting changes.
assumptions: Administrative actions may not be strongly bound to authenticated identity, timestamp, and change details in protected audit logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact repudiation subtree may differ.

title: Linkability of student and parent accounts via stored relationship links
description: The account directory stores explicit parent-child relationship links alongside account records. An attacker or unauthorized internal user who can access directory contents may correlate multiple accounts and activities, linking a child to one or more parents and linking family members across services or contexts.
assumptions: The directory persists relationship identifiers or references in a way that can be queried or inferred by parties beyond the minimum authorized set.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability through stored relational identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Identifiability of students and parents from account records
description: Writing account records into the directory may expose directly identifying attributes or stable identifiers for students and parents. If the directory is broadly accessible or insufficiently partitioned, individuals can be identified from the stored records.
assumptions: Account records contain names, usernames, emails, student IDs, parent IDs, or other direct or quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability from directory data.

title: Disclosure of sensitive family relationship data in the account directory
description: The grading service writes parent-child relationship links to the account directory. Unauthorized disclosure of these links reveals family associations and potentially educational status, which are sensitive personal data in many contexts.
assumptions: Relationship links are readable by administrators, other services, or users beyond those strictly needing access.

title: Disclosure of account records through overbroad directory access
description: If the account directory permits broad reads, synchronization, backup access, or administrative querying, account records written by the grading service may be exposed to unauthorized parties, revealing student and parent personal data.
assumptions: The directory is shared infrastructure and may be accessed by multiple services, operators, or support personnel.

title: Unawareness of storage and reuse of parent-child relationship links
description: Students and parents may be unaware that the grading service writes and persists family relationship links in the account directory, potentially for purposes beyond immediate grading workflows. This can undermine transparency about what data is stored and how it is reused.

title: Non-compliant propagation of educational and family data to the directory
description: The grading service may write more account or relationship data to the directory than is necessary, or do so without an appropriate legal basis, purpose limitation, or retention control. Because the data concerns students and parent-child relationships, this flow may violate privacy obligations if not properly governed.

title: Excessive disclosure of student and staff data to third-party host via full backup replication
description: The nightly replication sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to an external cloud hosting provider. This may disclose more personal data than is necessary for backup/hosting purposes, including sensitive educational records and directory information, to a third party.

title: Secondary use of replicated educational records by cloud provider
description: Once full backups and replicated hosting data are stored by the cloud provider, the provider could use grade records, assignments, or account-directory data for purposes beyond backup/hosting, such as analytics, service improvement, profiling, or operational reuse not expected by data subjects.

title: Linkability of student activity and identity across replicated datasets
description: Because the backup contains full grade records, assignments, and the account directory together, the cloud provider can link identities to coursework, performance history, and account attributes across datasets and over time, enabling richer correlation than any single dataset alone.

title: Identifiability of students and staff from full replicated backups
description: The account directory combined with assignments and grades makes individual students and staff directly identifiable within the hosted backup environment, even if some application-layer views would otherwise limit identification.
assumptions: The account directory includes direct identifiers or quasi-identifiers sufficient to single out individuals.

description: Shipping complete grade records, assignments, and directory data to an external hosting provider may violate data-minimization, purpose-limitation, retention, localization, contractual, or student-record protection obligations if not properly justified and governed.
assumptions: Applicable privacy, education-record, or contractual requirements restrict third-party transfers and require safeguards, minimization, and documented processor terms.

title: Unawareness of third-party backup replication by students and staff
description: Data subjects may be unaware that their grades, assignments, and account-directory data are replicated nightly to a cloud hosting provider, reducing transparency about where their educational records are stored and processed.
assumptions: Notices, consent flows, or privacy communications do not clearly explain this third-party replication arrangement.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact subtree may vary.

title: Insufficient auditability of backup transfer and provider handling
description: If the nightly backup and replication process lacks strong logging, receipts, or verifiable audit trails, the provider or sender may later be unable to prove what data was transferred, when it was accessed, or whether deletion/restore actions occurred, undermining accountability for personal-data handling.
assumptions: Transfer, access, restore, and deletion events are not all immutably logged and attributable across organizational boundaries.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for repudiation/accountability gaps in cross-boundary data transfer.

title: Grade records can be linked across student, parent, and teacher views
description: When the grading service reads the same grade records to construct multiple role-specific views, identifiers and stable record references may allow correlation of a student's performance data across contexts and recipients, enabling linkage of records that should remain context-separated.
assumptions: The service uses common identifiers or shared record keys when generating different views for students, parents, and teachers.

title: Role-specific views may reveal the existence of grade records
description: By reading grade records and presenting tailored views, the grading service may allow recipients to infer whether records exist for a particular student, assignment, or class even when they should not know that such records are present.

title: Overly detailed grading views may disclose personal academic information
description: The grading service may expose full grade records, comments, rubric details, or historical performance data to students, parents, or teachers beyond what each role needs, resulting in disclosure of personal data from the database.
assumptions: Access control or data minimization for role-based views is incomplete or misconfigured.

title: Users may be unaware that grade data is reused to generate multiple audience views
description: Students, parents, or teachers may not be informed that the same underlying grade records are processed and repurposed to build different views, reducing transparency about how personal academic data is used.
